papers.title_en: Look, Reason, Draw a Region: Recursive Refinement for Spatial Context Prediction
papers.authors: Wajeeha Tahir, Anna Tegon, Lionnus Kesting, Gamze İslamoğlu, Kristóf Karacs, Luca Benini, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson
papers.evidence: 面向空间上下文与空间关系预测的递归视觉语言推理
papers.tldr: 空间上下文预测需要视觉定位与空间推理，现有视觉语言模型在空间关系和物理约束上仍易出错。作者提出 Spatial-TRM：冻结视觉语言特征，用凸区域解码器和权重共享的递归推理器反复细化区域预测，仅11.2M可训练参数。在 RoboSpatial-Home 上取得29.51%上下文准确率，较同参数单步模型提升9.02个百分点（相对44.0%）。总参数877.8M，约为13B RoboPoint的1/15，表明固定可训练参数下递归细化能提升空间上下文预测。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial context prediction requires visual grounding and spatial reasoning to identify vacant regions relative to objects in a scene. Spatial relationships and physical constraints remain challenging for large vision-language models (VLMs). Recursive reasoning has demonstrated strong performance on discrete and abstract reasoning tasks, motivating its use for improving spatial context prediction in natural images. Weight sharing enables higher accuracy with a small trainable parameter count. We introduce Spatial-TRM, a compact recursive model with frozen vision-language features, a convex region decoder, and just 11.2M trainable parameters. This weight-tied reasoner supports six spatial relationships, three reference frames, and open-vocabulary anchor objects. On the RoboSpatial-Home benchmark, Spatial-TRM achieves 29.51% context accuracy, a gain of 9.02 percentage points (44.0% relative) over a separately trained single-step model with the same parameter count. Including the frozen encoders, the model has 877.8M total parameters, approximately $15\times$ fewer than the reported 13B size of RoboPoint. These results show that repeated refinement improves spatial context prediction from pretrained vision-language features at a fixed trainable parameter count on this benchmark.

papers.title_en: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
papers.authors: Rui Gong, Ruoyu Wang, Yalun Dai, Hao Li, Sidi Yang, Qihao Zhao, Hongyu Li, Zeyang Guan, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Kim-Hui Yap, Ziwei Liu
papers.evidence: 使用三维感知工具闭合证据回路的空间推理智能体
papers.tldr: 空间推理要求模型理解三维物体位置、关系与运动，现有智能体虽能调用3D工具，却常卡在“工具读对、模型答错”的证据到结论缺口。S-Agent 2.0把命令行感知工具包接入现成通用编程智能体，并以持久场景记忆和自然空间语言解释每个读数来闭合证据环。在MMSI-Bench和ReVSI上，它为Qwen3.8-27B带来+13.9和+20.5分提升，为Gemini-3.8-Flash带来+11.2和+9.6分提升，开放骨干下达到66.5和82.3。该设计保持编程智能体灵活性，使感知证据可积累、可解释并稳定转化为空间结论。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move. Agentic VLMs have recently brought large improvements on such tasks by letting the model actively gather evidence with 3D perception tools instead of answering in a single pass. Even so, on many questions the tools return the right evidence and the model still does not arrive at the correct answer: the gap between model and tools, where raw readings become usable conclusions, is left unfilled. We present S-Agent 2.0, a spatial reasoning agent that equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line perception toolkit, and we design the interface around one principle: help the VLM close the evidence loop: acquire scene evidence, remember it in a persistent scene memory, and interpret each reading in plain spatial language. This design keeps the full flexibility of a coding agent, and every reading it acts on stays grounded in the tools' geometry. On MMSI-Bench and ReVSI, the toolkit improves a strong open-source model, Qwen3.8-27B, by +13.9 and +20.5 points over the same agent without tools, and a strong closed-source model, Gemini-3.8-Flash, by +11.2 and +9.6 points. With the open backbone S-Agent 2.0 reaches 66.5 on MMSI-Bench and 82.3 on ReVSI, ahead of the specialized system SpatialClaw on the same backbone (62.6 and 74.5), and with Gemini-3.8-Flash it reaches 74.1 and 90.5 against its 67.0 and 79.7. Both tool gains shrink as the backbone grows more capable, but SpatialClaw's shrinks far more on ReVSI, from +13.2 to +2.7, while ours stays at +9.6. S-Agent 2.0 also works across different general coding agent harnesses, such as Codex and Claude Code.

papers.title_en: Cache Locally, Recompute Selectively for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.authors: Junhyeok Lee, Sangyoon Lee, Jaeho Lee
papers.evidence: 流式视频问答中的有界KV记忆与选择性重算
papers.tldr: 流式视频理解需低延迟处理持续视频流，现有预填充KV缓存方法因空闲期上下文受限产生上下文错配。FrameBlend无需训练，在查询时用查询相关上下文重预填充选定视频token并替换缓存KV。它在三个框架和五个基准上最高提升3.9个百分点，RVS-Ego每帧预填充FLOPs降超20%、总处理时间降14–59%。这表明重新分配空闲期与查询期的上下文计算可改善精度-效率权衡。
papers.abstract_en: Streaming video understanding (SVU) requires video-LLMs to process incoming video continuously while answering user queries with low latency. Recent methods reduce query-time cost by prefilling frames into KV caches during idle time and reusing the cached KVs at query time. To bound per-frame computation over unbounded video streams, these methods restrict the context available during prefill. This creates a fundamental context mismatch: the restricted context may omit information needed to properly contextualize video tokens, yet, still contain information irrelevant to the eventual query, which is unknown during prefill. We propose FrameBlend, a simple yet effective plug-and-play method to address this mismatch through selective KV recomputation, without requiring any additional training. At query time, FrameBlend re-prefills selected video tokens using query-relevant context and replaces their cached KVs with recomputed ones. Crucially, this recomputation enables shorter attention windows during idle-time prefill, substantially reducing prefill cost while improving accuracy. Experiments across three SVU frameworks and five streaming and offline benchmarks demonstrate accuracy gains of up to 3.9 pp. On RVS-Ego, FrameBlend reduces per-frame prefill FLOPs by over 20% and total processing time by 14-59% for retrieval-based frameworks, including the cost of query-time recomputation. These results demonstrate that a simple change in how contextualization is distributed between idle time and query time can improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for SVU.

papers.title_en: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
papers.authors: Yifan Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Xiaojun Ye, Yifei Liu, Donggang Li, Xiaolong Zhou, Zhihang Zhong, Xue Yang
papers.evidence: 3DFusionMemory将场景观测融合为可查询的空间关系记忆
papers.tldr: 空间推理不仅依赖几何工具，更需判断何时直接观察、何时重建、测量或切换参考系。SpatialBrain在固定视觉语言主干下，用3DFusionMemory融合场景观测为可查询空间关系，并用空间技能库与空间认知积累“何时如何调用”的过程经验。在五个空间推理基准中，四个优于同主干直接回答，一个持平。其意义在于将场景证据与推理经验分离，使智能体跨任务积累可迁移的空间决策能力。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

papers.title_en: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Qinfan Zhang, Yifan Luo, Haoyuan Shi, Guanlin Liu, Han Dong, Haozhe Shan, Yong Dai, Xiangcong Ren, Xiaozhu Ju
papers.evidence: 将几何词元维护为持久的时间空间记忆
papers.tldr: 多数VLA模型依赖当前2D观测，几何信息常随单帧推断后被丢弃，难以形成持久任务表征。GeoMem-VLA将显式3D监督内化为GeoPlan几何token，并作为时序记忆持续更新，与观测记忆检索融合以生成动作。在LIBERO达98.9%，RoboTwin清洁/随机化达91.10%/91.24%，五项真实任务平均78.0%。结果表明，内化并记忆3D场景理解可提升机器人控制。
papers.abstract_en: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.

papers.title_en: Retrieval-Augmented Online Textual Memory for Episodic Memory Video Question Answering
papers.authors: Raffaele Cali, Giuseppe Lando, Rosario Forte, Antonino Furnari
papers.evidence: 在线文本记忆与检索单元预算用于第一视角视频问答
papers.tldr: 长时第一视角视频难以压缩成可检索且保留问答证据的记忆。本文在在线文本记忆框架中系统比较检索单元、查询形式、上下文预算与重排策略，提出 Parent 配置：用细粒度字幕子块匹配后返回完整父字幕供推理。在 QAEgo4D-Closed 上取得 56.4% 准确率，仅暴露少量文本记忆即可匹敌全记忆与检索基线。分析表明提高检索预算虽提升 Hit@K 与 Recall@K，却可能因干扰项降低答案准确率，说明记忆检索应兼顾证据可靠性与判别性。
papers.abstract_en: Long egocentric videos pose a central challenge for multimodal language models: the visual stream must be compressed into a memory representation that can be searched efficiently while still preserving the evidence needed for question answering. Building on an online textual-memory framework in which first-person videos are converted into temporally grounded captions, this work systematically studies the role of retrieval in episodic-memory video question answering. We evaluate how different retrieval units, query formulations, context budgets, and reranking strategies affect multiple-choice answering on QAEgo4D-Closed, isolating retrieval as the main variable while keeping the underlying generated memory fixed.   Our best configuration, Parent, matches fine-grained caption subchunks, then provides their full parent captions to the reasoner. It achieves 56.4 % accuracy, matching strong full-memory and retrieval baselines while exposing only a small fraction of the textual memory at question time. More importantly, our analysis shows that better temporal coverage does not necessarily translate into better answers: increasing the retrieval budget improves temporal Hit@K and Recall@K, but can reduce accuracy by introducing visually plausible distractors and uncertain caption evidence. These findings suggest that retrieval-augmented egocentric memory should not be optimized only for evidence recall, but also for the reliability, specificity, and answer-discriminative value of the retrieved context. The study motivates more structured episodic memories that move beyond raw caption retrieval toward evidence-aware representations for long-form egocentric reasoning.

papers.title_en: RecallGS: Geometry-Grounded Recall for Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Thanh-Khoi Nguyen, Thien-Phuc Tran, Minh-Triet Tran
papers.evidence: 从观测历史中检索几何-语义证据以支撑流式场景理解
papers.tldr: 在线语义3DGS需从流式观测理解开放词汇场景，但现有方法依赖额外学习的3D网络补几何上下文，增加训练与运行开销。RecallGS将历史观测视为非参数几何-语义先验，通过CLIP检索、alpha合成权重筛选几何支持视图，并按高斯渲染足迹聚合语义特征。该方法在ScanNet与ScanNet++上取得较强语义分割性能并达2.48 FPS。其贡献在于无需额外学习分支即可从观测历史恢复几何-语义上下文。
papers.abstract_en: Online semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables open-vocabulary scene understanding from streaming observations. However, existing methods recover geometric context missing from image-derived semantic features using an additionally learned 3D network, incurring extra training and runtime overhead. We observe that such geometric-semantic evidence may already exist in the agent's observation history and can be retrieved rather than learned. Based on this insight, we introduce RecallGS (Geometry-Grounded Recall for Online Semantic Gaussian Splatting), a lightweight, training-free mechanism that treats past observations as a non-parametric geometric-semantic prior. RecallGS follows a recall-ground-fuse pipeline: CLIP retrieves relevant observations, alpha-compositing weights identify geometrically supported views, and aggregate their semantic features over each Gaussian's rendered footprint. On ScanNet and ScanNet++, RecallGS achieves strong semantic segmentation performance at 2.48 FPS, demonstrating that geometric-semantic context can be effectively recovered from observation history without an additional learned 3D branch.

papers.title_en: Point-Level Refinable Semantic Mapping for Spatial Understanding
papers.authors: Taimeng Fu, Yi Du, Zitong Zhan, Qiwei Du, Shaoshu Su, Zhipeng Zhao, Chen Wang
papers.evidence: 可随时间修正的三维语义图空间记忆
papers.tldr: 3D语义地图是机器人长期自主的空间记忆，但现有对象级地图多面向静态环境，采用只增不减的点积分，导致感知误差累积和旧点残留。本文提出在线可细化语义建图框架，用多视角时序证据更新每个对象点的置信度，并结合对象跟踪与重识别保持实例身份。实验在Replica和ScanNet上分别提升3.46%和2.55%，动态与噪声场景更稳健。该工作让对象级语义地图从单调累积转向持续修正，为对象导航和具身问答提供有效空间记忆。
papers.abstract_en: Open-vocabulary 3D semantic maps have emerged as a key spatial memory representation for long-horizon robot autonomy, enabling robots to reason about objects, their spatial relationships, and past observations across time. However, existing object-centric semantic maps are primarily designed for static environments and rely on an append-only point integration strategy, where newly observed points are accumulated but previously integrated points are rarely reevaluated. Consequently, perception errors accumulate over time, and outdated points persist after objects move or disappear. Although recent dynamic mapping methods update object-level representations in changing scenes, they do not explicitly revise noisy or obsolete points within each object. We propose an online refinable semantic mapping framework that continuously refines object representations through probabilistic point-level confidence updating. Each object point maintains a confidence score that is updated online using multi-view temporal evidence: consistent observations reinforce reliable points, while inconsistent segmentation masks, depth measurements, and visibility cues suppress spurious and outdated points. Combined with object tracking and re-identification to preserve instance identities under motion and relocation, our framework enables object-centric semantic maps to be continuously refined rather than monotonically accumulated. Experiments demonstrate improved mapping accuracy over the previous method by 3.46% on Replica and 2.55% on ScanNet, show robustness in dynamic environments and under perception noise, and provide an effective spatial memory for object navigation and embodied question-answering with success rates of 82.4% and 76.7%.

papers.title_en: STRIDE: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Driving Edge Cases
papers.authors: Lieqi Liu, Rui gao, Jia-Chen Gu, Wenbo Hu, Zhaobin Mo, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar, Wei Wang, Nanyun Peng
papers.evidence: 面向视觉语言模型的时序记忆与空间理解基准
papers.tldr: 自动驾驶不仅要感知周围物体，还要理解它们如何随时间移动和交互，但现有基准对复杂时空推理的覆盖仍不足。作者提出STRIDE，这是面向长尾、安全关键场景的以对象为中心基准，包含六类任务，并将多项选择判断与开放式VQA解释配对。评测12个模型后，最佳模型GPT-6-Astra的多选平均准确率仅43.4%，随机基线约20%。研究还发现，描述场景能力强并不等于安全判断准确，重建物体运动也比回忆历史位置更难。
papers.abstract_en: In autonomous driving, perceiving surrounding objects is not enough: failing to understand how they move and interact over time can lead to dangerous decisions. Evaluating vision-language models (VLMs) therefore requires testing whether they connect past spatial observations to future consequences. Yet existing benchmarks often assess edge cases through basic perception questions or test temporal understanding in simple scenarios, leaving complex spatiotemporal reasoning underexplored. We introduce STRIDE (SpatioTemporal Reasoning In Driving Edge Cases), an object-centric benchmark for long-tail, safety-critical driving scenarios. STRIDE covers six task families: spatial perception, spatial understanding, temporal memory, temporal extrapolation, trajectory prediction, and scene-context awareness. It pairs multiple-choice questions probing individual spatiotemporal judgments with related free-form visual question answering (VQA) requiring detailed scene explanations and justifications of driving decisions. We prioritize scenes with unusual object behaviors and complex traffic interactions, generate reference answers from structured dataset annotations through automated procedures, and use limited language-model assistance and human verification to ensure annotation quality. Across 12 proprietary, open-weight, and driving-specialized models, even the best performer, GPT-6-Astra, achieves only 43.4% average multiple-choice accuracy, versus an approximately 20% random-choice baseline. Further analysis reveals that strong performance in describing driving scenes does not necessarily translate to accurate safety-critical judgments, and that models struggle more with reconstructing object motion than recalling past positions. STRIDE thus exposes spatiotemporal driving limitations that aggregate VQA scores can conceal.

papers.title_en: A failure of Imagination: VLMs fail to use visual representations for text, but self-distillation can help
papers.authors: Shashwat Singh, He He, Tal Linzen
papers.evidence: 用配对文本与图像对照检验视觉对齐能否改善文字几何题
papers.tldr: 视觉语言模型能看图答题，却未必把视觉结构真正融入文本表征。作者构造图文等价的数图形任务，区分弱多模态与强多模态，并比较Qwen-2.5、Mistral及其视觉对齐版本。结果显示视觉对齐模型在纯文本题上并无优势，探针也未见更强视觉结构。作者提出自蒸馏目标，把上下文视觉嵌入对齐到文本嵌入，无需任务监督即可提升纯文本表现，表明VQA式对齐仍有跨模态迁移潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language (VL) models are typically built by fine-tuning a language model to attend to visual features in service of a Visual Question-Answering objective. We ask whether this alignment changes how language models represent text---especially on tasks where visualization would help, like geometry questions posed in words. We distinguish weak multimodality (the model can answer questions about an input image) from strong multimodality (the model's text representations themselves become vision-aligned, improving performance on text-only tasks with latent visual structure). To test for strong multimodality, we construct a task of shape-counting problems with paired equivalent text and image specifications. This task is trivial when the image is provided, but requires visualization when specified in text as line coordinates. We compare instruction-tuned Qwen-2.5 and Mistral models against their vision-aligned counterparts on the text variant of the task. We find that the multimodal models do no better in this setting, despite strong performance on the image version of the task. Probing experiments corroborate this: vision-aligned decoder embeddings carry no more visual structure than their text-only counterparts. Finally, we provide an optimization objective that distills in-context visual embeddings into text embeddings. This alignment induces gains on the text variant of the task without explicit task supervision, even on samples more complex than seen during alignment. This suggests that VQA-style alignment leaves available cross-modal transfer untapped.

papers.title_en: PanoGraphGS: Unifying Panoptic Segmentation and Hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs with Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Jinghan Gao, Siyu Wang, Dongyu Feng, Yiyuan Pan, Rong Xiong
papers.evidence: 跨视角一致的泛光语义与实例关联以构建三维场景图
papers.tldr: 构建语言引导导航所需的分层3D场景图，需要跨视角一致地区分语义区域与物体实例。PanoGraphGS在共享高斯几何上联合学习语义和实例特征，用原型语义学习与关联实例学习实现一致的全景预测，并构建floor-room-stuff-object层级及包含和空间关系。在Replica和NaviGS上，其物体节点准确率平均超过最强基线50个百分点以上，2D全景分割也达到评估方法中的最优。该工作统一了全景3D高斯表示与分层场景图构建，并发布NaviGS数据集。
papers.abstract_en: 3D scene graphs support language-guided navigation by organizing physical entities and their containment and spatial relations into hierarchical maps. Building such structured maps requires a scene representation that consistently distinguishes semantic regions and object instances across viewpoints. To this end, we present PanoGraphGS, a unified framework that integrates panoptic 3D Gaussian representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph construction. The framework learns semantic and instance features on shared Gaussian geometry. Prototype-based semantic learning and association-based instance learning produce consistent panoptic predictions across viewpoints. The learned representation supports novel-view panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level panoptic decoding. A semantic-aware scene graph module further recovers a floor-room-stuff-object hierarchy with containment and spatial relations. We further release NaviGS, a real-world dataset for panoramic scene understanding. The dataset provides 3DGS, mesh, RGB, semantic, and depth data. For 3D scene graph identification, PanoGraphGS outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline in object-node accuracy by more than 50\% points on average across Replica and NaviGS. PanoGraphGS also achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods in 2D panoptic segmentation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of PanoGraphGS in both hierarchical 3D scene understanding and 2D panoptic segmentation. The project website is available at: https://github.com/gaojh0333/PanoGraphGS.

papers.title_en: P$^3$-VLM: A Point-based Alternative for Grounded 3D Vision-Language Models
papers.authors: Anna-Maria Halacheva, Jan-Nico Zaech, Sombit Dey, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel
papers.evidence: 以3D点替代边界框作为几何表示提示
papers.tldr: 现有3D视觉语言模型评测与提示过度依赖边界框，边界框泄露类别信息，使模型可通过坐标捷径绕过视觉推理。作者提出以单点作为定位提示，并设计三通路P^3-VLM，融合位置、任务与上下文信息且无需检测器。在点位定位描述任务上达到52.1%的SOTA，并提升鲁棒性、OOD泛化与无定位3D VQA表现。该工作揭示并缓解了语义泄漏，强化了视觉-空间推理。
papers.abstract_en: Examining existing benchmarks for grounding in 3D VLMs reveals a pervasive "semantic leakage" in the evaluation and prompting protocols: a heavy reliance on bounding boxes as spatial prompts or representation primitives. Because bounding boxes are highly informative of object categories, they introduce a shortcut for the models to neglect visual information during 3D VLM training. We demonstrate this with a "blind" LLM that, prompted only with the box coordinates, can perform surprisingly well. To further analyze this shortcut, we propose point-based grounding prompting - querying models with a single 3D point instead of a box. Under this protocol, the accuracy of the blind LLM drops from 36.4% to 18.0% on ScanNet's Nr3D, and similarly degrades for 3D VLMs (e.g. LL3DA).   Building on this insight, we introduce P$^3$-VLM, a novel tri-pathway 3D VLM that supports point-based prompts and achieves 52.1% state-of-the-art accuracy on location-grounded captioning under this setting. To achieve this, we redesign the architecture while keeping it detector-free, scene-centric, and suitable for 3D GS inputs. P$^3$-VLM utilizes three complementary pathways (location-, task-, and context-aware), enabling strong reasoning about scenes without any bounding box dependencies. The key benefit of point-based learning is a consistent improvement across settings: P$^3$-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance under point-based grounding while also improving robustness, OOD generalization, and performance on ungrounded scene-centric 3D VQA benchmarks, reflecting its reduced reliance on bounding-box shortcuts and resulting stronger visual-spatial reasoning.

papers.title_en: GALA: Geometry-Aware Language Model for Controllable Object Arrangement
papers.authors: Chucheng Xiang, Runze Wang, Zhi Deng, Ruchao Bao, Yuanwei Zhang, Yuxuan Xie, Hanliu Wang, Liangzhen Fei, Wenzheng Wu, Cheng Wan, Peifeng Li, Zhongyuan Liu, Ligang Liu
papers.evidence: 将点云几何感知与文本指令对齐用于3D摆放
papers.tldr: 现有3D场景布局方法多依赖有向包围盒，难以推理支撑、包含等细粒度几何约束。GALA引入显式点云感知的几何感知语言模型，以场景上下文和放置指令为条件，自回归逐个预测目标物体6D位姿，并采用两阶段训练对齐几何与文本。实验表明其显著优于无显式几何推理的基线，还构建了多源场景数据集并开源，支持文本驱动场景生成。
papers.abstract_en: Reasoning about fine-grained placement constraints, such as support and containment, is essential for realistic 3D scene creation. It remains a significant challenge for existing methods that rely on simplified object representations like oriented bounding box (OBB), which are blind to the detailed geometry. To address this limitation, we introduce GALA, a geometry-aware language model with explicit point cloud perception for controllable object placement. Our model performs autoregressively by predicting the 6D pose of one target object at a time conditioned on the scene context and placement instruction. We utilize a two-stage training strategy: the first stage aligns geometric and textual modalities through pretraining tasks, and the second stage fine-tunes the model for placement. To facilitate this task, we also curate a multi-source scene dataset covering diverse room types and fine-grained furniture arrangements, which will be open-sourced for community benefit. Experiments on our benchmark show our model significantly outperforms baselines without explicit geometric reasoning. We further develop a multi-stage plan-place-verify agent pipeline that uses the model for text-driven scene generation. Project Page: https://xccelephant.github.io/paper/gala/

papers.title_en: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
papers.authors: Zhichao Zhai, Menglei Zhao, Guikun Chen, Zihao Yan, Kanzhi Wu, Wenguan Wang, Jun Xiao
papers.evidence: 语言模型在体素视图上编程以实现三维空间推理与物体放置
papers.tldr: 语言模型能生成程序，但在3D场景中执行空间指令仍需构造语言未明说的几何参照。VoxProg把3D物体放置转化为体素编程：模型在局部体素视图上生成程序，先定位任务相关表面区域，再测量几何并计算目标SE(3)位姿。执行反馈支持迭代修正代码，在71项VoxProg-Bench和外部基准上稳定优于关系、关键点与网格基线。
papers.abstract_en: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

papers.title_en: SpaceCache: Intermediate Feature Reuse for Efficient Semantic Segmentation on Point Cloud Streams
papers.authors: Dongheon Yang, Beomseok Kang, Jae-Joon Kim
papers.evidence: 免训练的跨帧特征缓存为重叠区域复用缓存token
papers.tldr: 点云流分割逐帧从头计算，但连续帧空间高度重叠，冗余明显。SpaceCache利用点云Transformer深层特征跨帧语义一致的特点，免训练缓存已观测区域token，使其跳过若干block并复用特征，仅算剩余token后恢复布局做稠密预测。在nuScenes、Waymo、ScanNet上配合Utonia与LitePT-B，最高1.65倍加速且mIoU下降不足1点，并优于token merging，为高效点云流分割提供可插拔复用方案。
papers.abstract_en: Point-cloud streams are central to autonomous driving and robotics, yet existing segmentation networks process every frame from scratch, although consecutive frames largely overlap. We observe that the intermediate features of point-cloud transformers remain semantically consistent across frames for the same spatial region, especially in deep stages. Building on this, we present SpaceCache, a training-free feature cache that reuses these features across frames. Tokens of previously observed regions skip a sequence of transformer blocks and take their cached features, only the remaining tokens are computed, and the full token layout is restored for dense prediction. Lightweight cache management keeps reused features reliable by limiting each entry's age and evicting low-confidence entries. Unlike token merging, SpaceCache selects tokens at negligible cost and runs its cache operations once per encoder stage. On both outdoor and indoor benchmarks, such as nuScenes, Waymo, and ScanNet, with two transformer backbones of Utonia and LitePT-B, SpaceCache achieves up to 1.65x speedup with less than 1-point mIoU drop and consistently outperforms token-merging methods.

papers.title_en: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
papers.authors: Dongjie Cheng, Ruifeng Yuan, Ran Wei, Ning Song, Yongqi Li, Wenjie Li
papers.evidence: 基于视觉语言模型的跨视角时空推理智能体
papers.tldr: 现有VLM需对运动、动作与视角变化做时空推理，但视频世界模型常以固定流程调用，难适配多样任务。CoWorld Reasoner将VWM作为统一视觉推理引擎，用工具暴露多种视觉操作，并以技能引导VLM决定是否想象、选择操作和解释视觉证据。它还引入VLM-VWM Harness协同演化，在冻结权重下依据执行反馈联合修订工具、技能与代码。七个基准均优于同VLM直接推理，MMSI和ERQA相对准确率分别提升11.8%和13.0%。
papers.abstract_en: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show. Video World Models (VWMs) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task-relevant visual content as additional evidence. However, existing approaches typically invoke a VWM through fixed pipelines centered on a predefined form of visual imagination, such as novel-view synthesis. To support flexible visual imagination for diverse reasoning tasks, we introduce CoWorld Reasoner, an agentic framework that uses a VWM as a unified visual reasoning engine. Its Video World Model-Driven Harness exposes multiple visual operations through tools and uses skills to guide the VLM in deciding whether to imagine, selecting an operation, constructing a generation request, and interpreting the resulting visual evidence. We further introduce VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution, which jointly revises tools, skills, and execution code based on execution feedback while keeping both model weights fixed. Across seven benchmarks spanning spatial intelligence, temporal and causal reasoning, and perceptual reasoning, CoWorld Reasoner outperforms direct reasoning with the same VLM. The strongest variant improves on all seven benchmarks, including relative accuracy gains of 11.8% on MMSI and 13.0% on ERQA, and outperforms all five evolving baselines using the same backbone across five benchmarks.

papers.title_en: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
papers.authors: Luozheng Qin, Yuhan Zhu, Changhai Zhou, Qian Qiao, Jun Gao, Yuhua Zhou, Harry Zhang, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuxuan Liu, Kaijie Chen, Andrew Chen, Pony Ma
papers.evidence: 面向空间关系、距离与放置判断的系统一多模态模型
papers.tldr: 空间智能需在交互频率下快速判断空间关系、距离与放置位置，但视觉语言模型依赖自回归文本生成，推理与解析开销大。MJev-Spatial 将选项、数值分箱和图像区域统一视为类别，利用骨干预训练查询与键投影打分，无需新增参数，单次前向即可完成选择、数值和点预测。基于 Qwen3.5-4B 在 1230 万问答对上训练，总体得分 65.64%，十二项基准全面超过原始自回归基模型，并显著加速。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial intelligence lets an agent perceive and act in the physical world, and many of its judgments must be made at interaction rates: which spatial relation holds, how far an object is, or where to place it. Vision-language models (VLMs) produce these answers by free-form text generation, paying for autoregressive decoding and answer parsing even though the output space is compact: one of a few options, a scalar, or a 2D point. In light of this, we introduce MJev-Spatial, a System 1 multimodal decision model that tackles all three types of spatial understanding tasks within a unified classification framework. Specifically, MJev-Spatial treats each candidate as a class and scores it using the backbone's pretrained query and key projections, without adding parameters. The candidates are the given options for choice tasks, or value bins and image regions refined through coarse-to-fine classification for numerical and point prediction, respectively. At inference, each classification decision takes a single forward pass and generates no answer tokens. To train on heterogeneous spatial data efficiently, we supervise all coarse-to-fine stages jointly with teacher forcing in one forward pass, and combine this with length-aware global batching and cross-GPU load balancing, raising training throughput by 30.8% over the original batching strategy. Built on Qwen3.5-4B and trained on 12.3M question-answer pairs converted from existing spatial datasets, MJev-Spatial achieves the highest overall score (65.64%) among eight tested models, ranks first on seven of twelve benchmarks, and outperforms its unmodified autoregressive base model on all twelve, while running 2.5 times faster than the fastest autoregressive baseline and 5.6 times faster than the base model.
